en: Book I Gate · Two paths
zh: 第一卷闸 · 两条路

en: Two boys grew under the same banyan; from there the roads divided.
zh: 同一棵榕树下长大的两个少年，从此走上了两条路。

en: The Brahmin prayer-syllable of “perfection,” murmured as if the heart were an arrow aimed at Brahman, is:
zh: 婆罗门祷文的音节「圆满」，默念它时如以心为箭指向梵天，其音为：

en: After three years in the forest, the elder who was hypnotised into bowing and blessing the two young men as they left is
zh: 林中度日三年，两个年轻人告别时被催眠得鞠躬祝福的长者是

en: After the teaching at Jetavana, the one who put on the yellow robe and entered the order is
zh: 祇园听法之后，披上黄衣、皈依僧团的是

en: The holy one to whose face Siddhartha said that doctrine cannot give awakening, and who at parting warned, “Beware of too much cleverness,” is
zh: 被悉达多当面指出「教义无法传达证悟」、临别赠言「提防你过分的聪明」的圣者是

en: The dialogue in which the two friends, divided in what they held true, at last went their separate ways is:
zh: 两位朋友由于理念不同，最终分道扬镳的那段对话剧情是：

en: Book II Gate · Awakening
zh: 第二卷闸 · 醒来

en: Twenty years were one dream of the world. What woke him was not another person, but a bird and a single syllable.
zh: 二十年尘世一梦，叫醒他的不是别人，是一只鸟和一个字。

en: The one who taught him the art of love, who at last set the little bird free from the golden cage and closed her gate to guests, is:
zh: 教他情爱之艺、最后放走金笼小鸟、闭门谢客的人是：

en: The rich merchant of the great city who tested his reading and writing, took him into trade, and could not sleep for gain and loss, is:
zh: 考校他读写、带他做生意、总为盈亏睡不着觉的大城富商是：

en: The gambling pieces with which, in his years of sinking, he staked fortunes to spend his contempt for money, are:
zh: 他沉沦岁月里一掷千金、借以发泄对金钱轻蔑的赌具是：

en: The creature that lay stiff and dead in the golden cage in his dream, and after which he woke and cast everything aside, is that:
zh: 梦中僵死在金笼里、让他惊醒后抛下一切的是那只：

en: In that instant by the river, the ancient syllable that called him back from the edge of death is:
zh: 河边那一瞬，把他从死亡边缘唤回的古老音节是：

en: The tale in which he died once by the river and lived again is called:
zh: 他在河边死过一回、又活过来的故事，叫作：

en: Book III Gate · The river
zh: 第三卷闸 · 河流

en: The one who learned from the river at last heard, among a thousand voices, the one.
zh: 向河水学习的人，终于听见了万千声音里的那一个。

en: The old ferryman who taught him to listen to the river, and at last walked into the woods and into oneness, is 〔 〕.
zh: 教他倾听河水、最后步入林中融入圆融的老船夫是〔 〕。

en: The child who stole the ferry-money from the two-coloured basket, broke the oar, and fled alone back to the city is 〔 〕.
zh: 偷走双色小篮里的船费、折断船桨、独自逃回大城的孩子是〔 〕。

en: When all voices became one, the word the river sang at last is 〔 〕.
zh: 万音归一，河水最终唱出的那个字是〔 〕。

en: The old monk who came to the ferry to be taught, kissed his friend's brow, and then saw all forms flowing, is 〔 〕.
zh: 在渡口求教、吻过老友前额之后看见万相流转的老僧是〔 〕。

en: The tale of two old men listening to the river side by side, when a thousand voices became the sound of perfection, is called “ ”.
zh: 两个老人并肩听河、万千声音汇成圆满之音的故事，叫作《 》。
